items.title: Run multiple AI image edits and keep designing while they load
items.excerpt: Figma's Jul 7 release note: designers can now fire off multiple AI image edits simultaneously from the toolbar and keep designing while they load — no more waiting for one edit to finish before starting the next. (Page dated 'Jul 7, 2026'; no per-entry permalink, entry title above.)

items.title: Meta built an AI detection tool to ID images and video created with its new models
items.excerpt: Meta previewed a web-based detector that reads Content Seal, the invisible watermark embedded in images made with its new Muse Image model (video via the upcoming Muse Video to follow). The mark survives cropping, compression and screenshots — but is incompatible with SynthID and C2PA Content Credentials, an interoperability headache for creatives.

items.title: Trimble adds AI tools to MEP estimating software
items.excerpt: Trimble baked AI into its MEP estimating tools: automatic drawing-scale/naming detection, AI symbol counting from construction drawings (3M+ symbols auto-detected, manual takeoff time cut 50–60%), auto-routed conduit length takeoff, and a natural-language AI Smart Assistant in Accubid Anywhere (80%+ time saved on historical-pricing research).

items.title: AutoRemesher 1.0: free tool automatically creates clean quad topology
items.excerpt: After five years of development, free MIT-licensed AutoRemesher reached 1.0, automatically converting high-poly meshes into clean quad-based topology on Windows/macOS/Linux — landing amid a surge of automated and AI-powered retopology tools (Tractive, CozyBlanket Pro, Sparseal). Note: algorithmic automation rather than ML-based — flag for curator.

items.title: Subscription now required for longer access to some Meta glasses features
items.excerpt: Meta now gates longer use of some smart-glasses features behind the $20/mo Meta One Premium subscription — including bigger monthly AI usage allowances, more image/video generations with advanced models, and 'Thinking' mode reasoning. Free users get 3 hours of Conversation Focus vs 15 for subscribers, sparking criticism since the feature runs locally.

items.title: Stop Naming CSS Variables After Colors
items.excerpt: 'A button does not need to know that it is blue': a case for semantic, purpose-driven design-token naming (palette vs semantic vs component tokens) across light/dark modes — the token hygiene that makes design systems machine- and AI-agent-readable. AI hook is implicit (token systems as AI source of truth); flag for curator.

items.title: Why your generated color palettes look muddy (and what OKLCH does about it)
items.excerpt: Why HSL-based palette generation produces muddy, uneven ramps and how the perceptually uniform OKLCH color space fixes it, with code examples and a free palette-generator tool. Craft/tooling piece; explicit AI angle is thin — flag for curator.
